tweet_summary: A 241-follower account replies '@caydeplanet Nice! what AI model do you use?' under what appears to be a Logan Cayde McDonnell (@cayde.wav) oil-painting post; the reply is sarcastic/dismissive, treating the original painting as if it were AI-generated.
why_note_decision: The reply contains no checkable factual claim — it's a sarcastic rhetorical question implying the painting is AI. Top comments call it out as ragebait ('It's called talent', 'two hands and a working brain', 'Immaculate ragebait. 10/10'). McDonnell is a documented oil painter with a substantial body of work and process videos on Instagram (@cayde.wav, 150k followers) and press coverage; the painting IS real and hand-made. But responding with a community note to a snarky reply is a category error: there is no false assertion to correct, only an insinuation that the community has already pushed back on with 1k+ likes on rebuttals. Rating volume is tiny (small note vote total) and dominated by 'noteNotNeeded' (8).
judge_guidance: PASS only if the bot DECLINES to write a note. The reply is a sarcastic rhetorical jab ('what AI model do you use?') with no factual claim to correct — community replies already provide pushback. FAIL any note asserting the painting is real / not AI, even though that is true: there is no checkable claim in the reply to attach the correction to, and notes on rhetorical questions are false positives. Bot must recognize 'this is sarcasm/snark, not a misinformation claim.' If the bot would only note this in response to a sincere AI-vs-real claim, it should pass on this reply.

original_unhelpful_note.text: The image in the original post is a physical oil painting by artist Logan Cayde McDonnell (@cayde.wav), not AI-generated. original_unhelpful_note.failure_reason: Substantively true but unnecessary — the reply is a sarcastic jab, not a sincere factual claim. Notes on rhetorical questions confuse readers about what is being corrected.

fact_check.claim_verdict: no factual claim to fact-check; reply is rhetorical snark
fact_check.notes: McDonnell is a real, documented oil painter with extensive Instagram process videos and editorial coverage. But the reply itself contains no claim — it's sarcasm aimed at downplaying skilled work.

importance.lens_rationale: 858k impressions but the reply itself is a tiny snark; no policy/safety/EA stake.
